div.div: Model calls take about 15 s [calc] of an illustrative 20 s [I8] task and carry all its tokens; caching cuts a repeat vision call to about 35 % [calc]
A WHERE ONE ILLUSTRATIVE TASK'S TIME GOES (bar lengths to scale, 55 px per second)

vision: confirm, tap again if needed
6 s [I4]

Model calls: 5 [I9] calls, 2 + 5 + 6 + 2 s = 15 s [calc] | device side: 0.1 + 2 + 1 + 2 s = 5.1 s [calc] | total 20.1 s [calc], about 20 s [I8]
Input tokens: 4 000 + 7 000 + 2 x 7 000 + 4 000 = 29 000 [calc], about 30 000 [I10] -> latency work starts with FEWER CALLS (e.g. the actuator's one OS call, diagram 02), not faster ones.
B ONE VISION CALL IN BASE-INPUT-TOKEN UNITS (bar lengths to scale) split [I7]

first 5 500 tok READ from the cache:
5 500 x 0.1 [P13] = 550 units
2 425 ÷ 7 000 = 35 % of the uncached call [calc]. The first call of a task pays the 1.25x write on the whole prefix; caching pays back from the second call on.

C1 THE CACHING RULES (public docs)
- The prefix order is fixed: tools -> system -> messages.
- Up to 4 breakpoints [P14] per request: one after tools + system, the rest on the latest tool results, advanced each turn.
- Lifetime 5 min [P15] by default, refreshed by each use; 1 h [P16] optional, written at 2x [P12].
- Any change at or before a breakpoint misses everything after it.

C2 WHY PRUNING BREAKS CACHING, AND THE FIX
Dropping the oldest screenshot edits an EARLY block, so every later block misses.
Fix: prune in batches. Keep the last 3 [P17] screenshots and prune every 25 [P18] turns, so the prefix stays byte-identical between prunes.
A 20 s [I8] task fits easily in the 5 min [P15] lifetime; long gaps between tasks let it expire.

C3 MODEL TIERS PER ROLE
One same-generation pair: fast tier $1, stronger tier $3 per million input tokens [P19]. Output price = 5x input [P20].
Strong tier on the orchestrator only (a wrong route wastes a whole turn); fast tier on the many specialist calls.
Outputs here are short tool calls, so input tokens dominate: caching matters more than reply length.

Legend: green bar = model-call time | blue bar = device-side time | grey = uncached input tokens | light green = cache read | amber = cache write | red tick = cache breakpoint. Units in B = tokens x price multiplier, i.e. cost relative to base input price.

Sources. Numbers are loaded from ../constants.json by key (shown). P = public (cited doc/paper, value as published); I = illustrative (round value chosen to explain the idea, never a measurement); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/07-cost-and-latency.md (illustrative budget table, caching arithmetic, tiers). Public rules and multipliers: prompt-caching documentation (prefix order, breakpoints, lifetimes, price table read 2026-11 - prices change, multipliers are the durable part); computer-use tool documentation, 'Manage screenshot history'.

[I7] vision_call_tokens_illustrative = {total: 7000, stable_prefix: 3000, history: 2500, new_screenshot: 1500} input tokens. illustrative split used in the 07 caching arithmetic; new_screenshot chosen inside cu_tokens_per_screenshot
[I8] task_wall_time_illustrative = 20 s. illustrative end-to-end time for a simple 'open an app' task; sum of the 07 budget table
[I9] task_model_calls_illustrative = 5 calls. illustrative: 2 orchestrator + 3 vision calls in the 07 budget table
[I10] task_input_tokens_illustrative = 30 000 tokens. illustrative: 29 000 in the 07 budget table, rounded

[P13] cache_read_multiplier = 0.1 x base input price. public: Anthropic prompt-caching documentation, price table notes (standard multiplier)

[P15] cache_ttl_default = 5 min. public: Anthropic prompt-caching documentation
[P16] cache_ttl_long = 1 h. public: Anthropic prompt-caching documentation
[P17] cu_screenshots_kept = 3 screenshots. public: Anthropic computer-use tool documentation, 'Manage screenshot history' (suggested default)
[P18] cu_prune_interval = 25 turns. public: Anthropic computer-use tool documentation, 'Manage screenshot history' (suggested default)
